title: Square-zero infinitesimal points of a group space form a module
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $G$ be a group algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with identity $e:S\to G$, multiplication and inverse satisfying the group identities; commutativity and smoothness are not assumed. Let $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a first order thickening of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], defined by an ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$, so $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Write $G(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,G)$, $e_T$ for its identity, $e_0:T_0\to S\xrightarrow{e}G$, and $K=\ker(G(T)\to G(T_0))$. Let $\Omega^1_{G/S}$ denote the sheaf of relative Kahler differentials on the small etale site: it represents $S$-derivations from the structure sheaf into module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; let $e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S}$ be its tensor pullback to $T_0$, and $\widetilde I$ the module sheaf associated to the $A/I$-module $I$. There is a canonical additive-group isomorphism $$K\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S},\widetilde I).$$ It sends $e_T$ to zero and the product of two elements of $K$ to the sum of their images. Thus $K$ has a canonical $A/I$-module structure with its original group law as addition, and for every integer $r\geq0$ the pointwise $r$th-power map on $K$ is scalar multiplication by $r$.

proof.text: Multiplication by $A$ on $I$ factors through $A/I$: two lifts of a scalar differ by an element of $I$, whose product with $I$ is zero. Apply [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] with $X=G$, $a=e_T$ and $\mathcal J=\widetilde I$. Its hypotheses require only a first order thickening and the chosen lift, both supplied here. The set $L_G(e_0)$ is exactly $K$. We obtain a canonical pointed bijection $\delta:K\to M$, where $M=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{T_0}}(e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S},\widetilde I)$, and $\delta(e_T)=0$. This step does not assume local finite presentation or smoothness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization] also to $P=G\times_SG$, with chosen lift $(e_T,e_T)$ and reduction $(e_0,e_0)$. Write $M_P$ for its module of differences. The two projections induce $A/I$-linear maps $q_1,q_2:M_P\to M$. The combined map $q=(q_1,q_2):M_P\to M\times M$ is bijective: the pointed bijections of the cited lemma identify it with the bijection $L_P((e_0,e_0))\to K\times K$ sending a map to its two projections, whose inverse pairs the maps. Hence $q$ is a linear isomorphism. Indeed $q^{-1}(v+w)=q^{-1}(v)+q^{-1}(w)$ and $q^{-1}(cv)=cq^{-1}(v)$ follow by applying the injective linear map $q$ to the two sides. Postcomposition by $m:P\to G$ induces a linear map $m_*:M_P\to M$ by the same cited lemma. Thus $F=m_*q^{-1}:M\times M\to M$ is linear, and naturality gives $\delta(xy)=F(\delta(x),\delta(y))$. No product formula for differentials or choice of etale coordinates has been assumed.

proof.text: The two unit identities determine $F$. For $v\in M$, let $x=\delta^{-1}(v)$. The preceding naturality calculation and $m(x,e_T)=x$ give $F(v,0)=v$; similarly $m(e_T,x)=x$ gives $F(0,v)=v$. Linearity now gives $F(v,w)=F((v,0)+(0,w))=v+w$. Consequently $\delta(xy)=\delta(x)+\delta(y)$ for every $x,y\in K$. This is precisely the argument of Stacks Tag 0BF5, with the linearity justified in step 2 for arbitrary square-zero coefficients rather than only residue-field tangent vectors.

source.place: Tag 0BF5 (lemma-group-scheme-addition-tangent-vectors), proof by linearity and the two unit identities; agent extension to arbitrary square-zero ideals using steps 1 and 2.

proof.text: The bijection $\delta$ preserving identity and products identifies $K$ with the additive abelian group of $M$ (and sends inverses to negatives). Transfer the $A/I$-module action by $c\cdot x=\delta^{-1}(c\delta(x))$. Each module identity follows after applying $\delta$; its addition is the original multiplication on $K$. For powers, induction gives $\delta(x^0)=\delta(e_T)=0$ and $\delta(x^{r+1})=\delta(x^r)+\delta(x)=(r+1)\delta(x)$. Thus the $r$th-power map is scalar multiplication by $r$, including $r=0$. The construction uses only the fixed identity section and the canonical difference maps, so is canonical.
